name: Tulsi
description: An aromatic sacred herb widely grown in Indian households and temples.
medicinalUse: Helps with cough, cold, sore throat and mild fever.
emergencyUse: Chew washed leaves or prepare a warm infusion for mild cough.
precautions: Traditional medicinal use only. Avoid excessive use during pregnancy without medical advice.

name: Neem
description: A fast-growing tree valued for its bitter leaves and antibacterial properties.
medicinalUse: Used traditionally for skin conditions, acne and minor wounds.
emergencyUse: Crushed leaf paste can be applied on minor insect bites for relief.
precautions: Do not ingest neem oil undiluted. Not recommended for pregnant women.

name: Aloe Vera
description: A succulent plant whose gel is popular for skin and digestive care.
medicinalUse: Soothes minor burns, sunburn and dry skin.
emergencyUse: Apply fresh gel directly on minor burns after cooling the area with water.
precautions: Avoid oral consumption without guidance; may cause allergic reaction in some people.

name: Ashwagandha
description: A traditional adaptogenic shrub used in Ayurveda for stress relief.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used to reduce stress and improve energy levels.
emergencyUse: Not for emergency use; consult a practitioner for dosage.
precautions: Avoid during pregnancy and with sedative medication without medical advice.

name: Giloy
description: A climbing shrub known as 'Amrita' in Ayurveda for immunity support.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used to boost immunity and reduce fever.
emergencyUse: A lukewarm decoction may help ease mild fever symptoms.
precautions: Consult a doctor if fever persists beyond 2 days.

name: Brahmi
description: A creeping herb traditionally associated with memory and cognitive support.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used to support memory and mental clarity.
emergencyUse: Not for emergency use.
precautions: May interact with thyroid medication; consult a doctor.

name: Amla
description: Indian gooseberry tree, fruit rich in Vitamin C.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used to boost immunity and improve digestion.
emergencyUse: Fresh amla juice may help soothe mild acidity.
precautions: High acidity may not suit people with ulcers.

name: Turmeric
description: A rhizomatous herb widely used as a spice and traditional antiseptic.
medicinalUse: Used traditionally for inflammation and wound healing.
emergencyUse: A pinch of turmeric powder can be applied on minor cuts as an antiseptic.
precautions: May interact with blood-thinning medication.

name: Ginger
description: An aromatic rhizome commonly used in cooking and traditional remedies.
medicinalUse: Helps relieve nausea, cold and digestive discomfort.
emergencyUse: Warm ginger tea can help ease mild nausea or cold symptoms.
precautions: Avoid large doses if on blood thinners or with gallstones.

name: Mint (Pudina)
description: A fragrant herb commonly used for digestive and cooling remedies.
medicinalUse: Helps relieve indigestion, bloating and bad breath.
emergencyUse: Chewing fresh mint leaves can help relieve mild nausea.
precautions: Excess use may worsen acid reflux in sensitive individuals.

name: Curry Leaf
description: A small aromatic tree whose leaves are a staple South Indian seasoning.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used to support digestion and hair health.
emergencyUse: Not for emergency use.
precautions: No major precautions at culinary quantities.

name: Lemongrass
description: A fragrant grass used in teas and traditional remedies.
medicinalUse: Used traditionally to relieve stress and mild digestive issues.
emergencyUse: Lemongrass tea may help ease mild stomach discomfort.
precautions: May lower blood pressure; caution for hypotensive individuals.

name: Fenugreek (Methi)
description: An annual herb whose seeds and leaves are used in cooking and remedies.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used to manage blood sugar and lactation support.
emergencyUse: Soaked fenugreek seeds may help mild digestive discomfort.
precautions: May lower blood sugar; caution for diabetics on medication.

name: Hibiscus
description: A flowering shrub whose petals are used in hair and herbal tea remedies.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used for hair health and mild blood pressure support.
emergencyUse: Not for emergency use.
precautions: May interact with blood pressure medication.

name: Marigold (Genda)
description: A bright flowering plant used in traditional wound care.
medicinalUse: Used traditionally for minor cuts and skin inflammation.
emergencyUse: Petal paste may be applied on minor scrapes after cleaning the wound.
precautions: Avoid on deep or infected wounds; seek medical care.

name: Basil (Sweet Basil)
description: A culinary herb related to Tulsi with mild medicinal properties.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used for mild respiratory relief.
emergencyUse: Warm basil-leaf tea may help ease a mild cough.
precautions: Avoid excessive use in pregnancy.

name: Peepal
description: A large sacred fig tree found across Indian temples and roadsides.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used for asthma and skin conditions.
emergencyUse: Not for emergency use.
precautions: Consult a practitioner before internal use.

name: Banyan
description: India's national tree, known for its aerial roots and shade.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used for diabetes and skin ailments.
emergencyUse: Not for emergency use.
precautions: Not a substitute for prescribed diabetes medication.

name: Bael
description: A sacred tree whose fruit is used in traditional digestive remedies.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used for digestive disorders like diarrhea.
emergencyUse: Bael fruit pulp is traditionally used to ease mild diarrhea.
precautions: Avoid unripe fruit which may cause constipation.

name: Shatavari
description: A climbing plant traditionally used for women's health.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used to support women's reproductive health.
emergencyUse: Not for emergency use.
precautions: Consult a doctor during pregnancy or hormonal treatment.

name: Guduchi (see Giloy)
description: Alternate name for Giloy, used interchangeably in Ayurveda.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used to boost immunity.
emergencyUse: A lukewarm decoction may help mild fever.
precautions: Consult a doctor if symptoms persist.

name: Vasaka (Adulsa)
description: A shrub traditionally used for respiratory relief.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used for cough, bronchitis and asthma relief.
emergencyUse: Warm Vasaka leaf decoction may help ease a persistent cough.
precautions: Avoid during pregnancy without medical supervision.

name: Arjuna
description: A large tree whose bark is prized in Ayurvedic heart care.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used to support heart health.
emergencyUse: Not for emergency use.
precautions: Not a substitute for cardiac medication; consult a cardiologist.

name: Sandalwood (Chandan)
description: A fragrant tree whose wood paste is used in skincare.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used to cool skin and reduce acne.
emergencyUse: Sandalwood paste may be applied to cool minor skin irritation.
precautions: Patch test recommended to rule out allergy.

name: Henna (Mehendi)
description: A shrub whose leaves are used for dye and traditional cooling remedies.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used to cool the body and condition hair.
emergencyUse: Paste may be applied to soothe minor skin heat rashes.
precautions: Avoid on broken skin or open wounds.

name: Coriander (Dhania)
description: A common culinary herb with mild digestive benefits.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used to relieve bloating and mild indigestion.
emergencyUse: Coriander seed water may help ease mild stomach discomfort.
precautions: Generally safe at culinary doses.

name: Cumin (Jeera)
description: A widely used spice seed with digestive properties.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used to relieve gas and indigestion.
emergencyUse: Roasted cumin water may help relieve mild bloating.
precautions: Generally safe at culinary doses.

name: Fennel (Saunf)
description: An aromatic seed commonly chewed after meals in India.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used to aid digestion and freshen breath.
emergencyUse: Chewing fennel seeds may help relieve mild bloating.
precautions: Generally safe at culinary doses.

name: Clove (Laung)
description: A flower bud spice known for its numbing, antiseptic property.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used for toothache relief.
emergencyUse: A clove placed near an aching tooth may provide temporary relief.
precautions: Avoid prolonged contact with gums; seek a dentist for lasting pain.

name: Cinnamon (Dalchini)
description: An aromatic bark spice with traditional metabolic benefits.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used to support blood sugar balance.
emergencyUse: Not for emergency use.
precautions: Excess intake may affect liver in sensitive individuals.

name: Black Pepper (Kali Mirch)
description: A pungent spice vine used to enhance nutrient absorption.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used for cold, cough and digestion.
emergencyUse: A pinch of pepper with honey may help ease a mild cough.
precautions: Avoid large quantities on an empty stomach.

name: Holy Basil Krishna Tulsi
description: A purple-leaved variety of Tulsi with similar medicinal use.
medicinalUse: Helps with respiratory and immunity support.
emergencyUse: Warm Krishna Tulsi tea may help mild cold symptoms.
precautions: Same precautions as Tulsi.

name: Papaya Leaf
description: Leaves of the papaya tree, studied for platelet support.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used to support platelet count during dengue recovery.
emergencyUse: Not a treatment for dengue; seek medical attention immediately for dengue symptoms.
precautions: Never replace medical treatment for dengue with home remedies.

name: Moringa (Drumstick)
description: A nutrient-dense tree often called the 'miracle tree'.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used for nutrition and mild inflammation support.
emergencyUse: Not for emergency use.
precautions: May interact with blood pressure or thyroid medication.

name: Guava Leaf
description: Leaves of the guava tree used in traditional digestive remedies.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used to ease mild diarrhea.
emergencyUse: Boiled guava leaf water may help ease mild loose motions.
precautions: Seek medical care if diarrhea persists beyond 2 days.

name: Bougainvillea
description: An ornamental flowering shrub with mild traditional cough remedies.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used for cough relief in some folk remedies.
emergencyUse: Not for emergency use.
precautions: Limited scientific evidence; use with caution.

name: Lantana
description: A widespread flowering shrub, some traditional external uses.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used externally for skin infections in folk medicine.
emergencyUse: Not for emergency use — leaves and berries are toxic if ingested.
precautions: Toxic if ingested; keep away from children and pets.

name: Vetiver (Khus)
description: A fragrant grass root used for cooling drinks and mats.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used to cool the body in summer.
emergencyUse: Khus-infused water may help relieve mild heat exhaustion discomfort.
precautions: Not a substitute for medical care in heatstroke.

name: Indian Borage (Ajwain Patta)
description: A thick-leaved herb traditionally used for children's cough.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used for cough and cold in children.
emergencyUse: Warm leaf juice with honey may help ease a child's mild cough.
precautions: Consult a pediatrician before giving to infants.

name: Custard Apple Leaf
description: Leaves of the custard apple tree used in folk skin remedies.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used for minor skin infections and lice.
emergencyUse: Not for emergency use.
precautions: Seeds are toxic; avoid ingestion.

name: Drumstick Flower Moringa Flower
description: The flowers of the moringa tree, used in traditional nutrition.
medicinalUse: Traditionally valued for iron and nutrition support.
emergencyUse: Not for emergency use.
precautions: Generally safe in food quantities.

name: Indian Sarsaparilla (Anantmul)
description: A climbing root herb used in traditional cooling tonics.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used as a blood purifier and coolant.
emergencyUse: Not for emergency use.
precautions: Consult a practitioner for appropriate dosage.

name: Country Mallow (Bala)
description: A shrub used in Ayurvedic formulations for strength.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used to support strength and respiratory health.
emergencyUse: Not for emergency use.
precautions: May interact with heart medications; consult a doctor.

name: Indian Gooseberry Tree see Amla
description: Same as Amla, listed for alternate common name recognition.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used to boost immunity.
emergencyUse: Fresh juice may help soothe mild acidity.
precautions: High acidity may not suit people with ulcers.

name: Wood Apple (Kaith)
description: A tree whose fruit pulp is used in traditional digestive tonics.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used to relieve mild diarrhea and dysentery.
emergencyUse: Ripe pulp may help ease mild digestive upset.
precautions: Avoid unripe fruit which can be highly acidic.

name: Indian Long Pepper (Pippali)
description: A pungent vine fruit used in traditional respiratory remedies.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used for cough, cold and respiratory support.
emergencyUse: Pippali powder with honey may help ease a mild cough.
precautions: Avoid high doses during pregnancy.

name: Malabar Nut see Vasaka
description: Alternate name for Vasaka, a respiratory support shrub.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used for bronchitis and cough.
emergencyUse: Warm leaf decoction may ease a persistent cough.
precautions: Avoid during pregnancy without supervision.

name: Indian Aloe see Aloe Vera
description: Alternate listing for Aloe Vera.
medicinalUse: Soothes minor burns and dry skin.
emergencyUse: Apply fresh gel directly on minor burns.
precautions: Avoid oral use without guidance.

name: Spiny Gooseberry (Karonda)
description: A thorny shrub whose sour berries are used in traditional remedies.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used to relieve mild indigestion.
emergencyUse: Ripe berries may help ease mild digestive discomfort.
precautions: Unripe fruit can be very sour and irritate the stomach.

name: Indian Sorrel (Ambadi)
description: A hibiscus relative used for tangy teas and mild remedies.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used to support digestion and hydration.
emergencyUse: Cool ambadi tea may help relieve mild heat discomfort.
precautions: May lower blood pressure; caution advised.

name: Betel Leaf (Paan)
description: A heart-shaped leaf vine widely chewed and used medicinally.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used for digestion and minor mouth ailments.
emergencyUse: A washed betel leaf may be chewed to ease mild indigestion.
precautions: Avoid with tobacco or areca nut, which carry health risks.

name: Shami Tree
description: A drought-resistant tree sacred in desert regions of India.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used for skin ailments and cough.
emergencyUse: Not for emergency use.
precautions: Limited scientific validation; use cautiously.

name: Indian Coral Tree (Pangara)
description: A tree with coral-red flowers used in traditional joint remedies.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used for joint pain and intestinal worms.
emergencyUse: Not for emergency use.
precautions: Consult a practitioner; seeds may be toxic.

name: Kalmegh
description: A bitter herb known as 'King of Bitters' in Ayurveda.
medicinalUse: Traditionally used for fever and liver support.
emergencyUse: A mild Kalmegh decoction may help ease early fever symptoms.
precautions: Avoid during pregnancy; very bitter, may upset empty stomach.
